Paper_Metadata.Paper_Title: Revealing the oxidation growth mechanism and crack evolution law of novel Si-HfO2/Yb2Si2O7/Yb2SiO5 environmental barrier coatings during thermal cycling

Raw_Evidence_Span: Section 3.1 Microstructure and composition of feedstock and as-sprayed coating

Composition_Nominal.Original_Values: Yb2O3 and SiO2 powders mixed at 1:1 ratio
Yb2O3 and SiO2 powders mixed at 1:2 ratio

Process_Text.original: Si-HfO2/Yb2Si2O7/Yb2SiO5 EBC samples were deposited on the surface of 15 mm x 15 mm bulk SiCf/SiC substrates via PS-PVD method. Yb2O3 and SiO2 powders were mixed at 1:1 and 1:2 ratios, ball-milled (450 r/min, 7 h), dried, and subjected to solid-state reaction (1400 C, 2 h) to synthesize Yb2SiO5 and Yb2Si2O7 initial powders. Si-HfO2 powders were produced by blending 15 mol% HfO2 with 85 mol% Si, ball-milling at 500 r/min for 12 h, then drying. Three initial powders were processed into feedstocks via spray granulation. Trilayer EBC was fabricated via PS-PVD.
Process_Text.simplified: Feedstock synthesis: Yb2Si2O7 and Yb2SiO5 from Yb2O3+SiO2 solid-state reaction at 1400C/2h; Si-HfO2 from 85mol%Si+15mol%HfO2 ball-milled 500rpm/12h. Spray granulation to spheroidal feedstocks. PS-PVD deposition of trilayer EBC on SiCf/SiC substrate.

Structure_Text.original: The thicknesses of Si-HfO2, Yb2Si2O7, and Yb2SiO5 layers were ~40, ~119, and ~75 um, respectively. This tri-layer coating presented a dense structure, tight adhesion to CMC substrate, and no apparent cracks appeared in the coating layers and layer interfaces. The internal stress within the as-sprayed coating was a compressive stress of 257 MPa. Within Yb2Si2O7 layer, a small amount of light gray lamellar secondary phase (likely minor Yb2SiO5 phase from feedstock). For Yb2SiO5 layer, a small amount of dark gray lamellar secondary phase (Yb2O3 and SiO2 striped bands from dissociation in plasma). The porosity of the coating surface was 3.68%.
Structure_Text.simplified: Trilayer EBC: Si-HfO2 (~40 um) / Yb2Si2O7 (~119 um) / Yb2SiO5 (~75 um). Dense, tight adhesion, no cracks. Internal compressive stress 257 MPa. Surface porosity 3.68%.

Coating_Layer_Details.Microstructure_Features: Uniform mixture of Si and HfO2 phases; minor composition segregation areas do not detract from overall uniformity
Typical layered microstructure; small amount of light gray lamellar secondary phase (minor Yb2SiO5); a few encapsulated pores from gas entrapment during PS-PVD

Typical layered microstructure; small amount of dark gray lamellar secondary phase (Yb2O3 and SiO2 striped bands and Yb2SiO5 splats alternately); composed of fully melted and partially melted particles

Structure_Text.original: Phase I identified as X2-Yb2SiO5 with simple monoclinic structure (P21/C, space group#13) along [011] zone, interplanar spacing 5.483 A. Phase II confirmed as beta-Yb2Si2O7 with base-centered monoclinic structure (C2/m, space group#15) along [202], interplanar spacing 1.781 A. Twins and dislocations observed in Yb2Si2O7 layer. (001) twinning and [110] dislocations identified. Interaction zones between twinning and dislocations observed.
Structure_Text.simplified: Yb2Si2O7/Yb2SiO5 interface: X2-Yb2SiO5 (monoclinic P21/C) and beta-Yb2Si2O7 (monoclinic C2/m). (001) twins and [110] dislocations in Yb2Si2O7.

Twinning.Note: First observation of (001) twinning in Yb2Si2O7; previously only (110) twins reported; attributed to higher thermal stresses from higher cycling temperatures

Dislocations.Note: Combination of edge and screw dislocations identified via two-beam diffraction with g vectors [1-1-1], [20-1], [110], [021]

Twin_Dislocation_Interaction.Description: Interaction zones between (001) twinning and dislocations observed for the first time in Yb2Si2O7
Twin_Dislocation_Interaction.Mechanism: Edge dislocations reacting with twin boundaries generate new edge dislocations; incomplete dislocations on twin boundary can slip along the twin boundary

Composition.Note: m-TGO composed of SiO2 + HfSiO4 + HfO2; composition same as item_01 bond coat after oxidation
